It is 1923 and the era of silent ‘The Innsmouth Terror’ will be a full-length three-act glamorous dame kidnapped by a tentacled monstrosity. / The Innsmouth Terror is a classic 1920s scenario for 7th edition, perfect for those looking for a pick-up-and-play Arkham County. Designed for three to five players, it can to two sessions (4-8 hours). / The booklet contains:

rows.source_first_blocks: “We shall swim out to that brooding reef in the sea and dive down through black abysses to Cyclopean and many-columned Y’ha-nthlei, and in that lair of the Deep Ones we shall dwell amidst wonder and glory for ever.” / —H.P. Lovecraft, The Shadow over Innsmouth / INTRODUCTION

Keeper / KEEPER INFORMATION / The town of Innsmouth is a strange place. New England society has done its level best to ignore and forget this decrepit seaside village. Once a thriving port town, these days the harbor is full of silt, and only local fishing boats come and go with the tide. The train connection was abandoned not long after it was opened, the operators calling it the ‘least profitable line’ they had ever serviced. No one wanted to go to Innsmouth. And no one ever seemed to leave.

Keeper / THE INNSMOUTH TERROR / Technology is changing rapidly! Moving pictures are the latest big thing and there is a rush to develop color in film. While postproduction coloring has been around for a while, the dream has always been to capture color in real time. In 1923, technicolor refers to a prism beam-splitting system, where two black and white films are recorded simultaneously, one behind a red filter, and another behind a green filter. The process is complex, prone to slipping out of alignment and, at best, finicky. Production constantly must stop while the engineer fixes and tinkers with the single camera capable of this feat.

DRAMATIS PERSONAE / Genevieve ‘Ginny’ Dubois, age 25, starlet In bad light, one might mistake Ginny’s too-wide eyes and stretched-out smile for innocent beauty. But once the lights are shining and the cameras are rolling, only the thick makeup and dramatic angles can hide her slow transformation into a hybrid. She is determined to ‘hit it big’ before her transformation takes hold and will go to any lengths to make it so. Born in Innsmouth to a loving mother and a terrifying, Deep One father in 1897. It was assumed that one day, Ginny would join her brothers and sisters down below. However, Ginny had other plans. After running off with the family gold to study Theatre, she bought her way into various productions at the Miskatonic Playhouse. Sponsoring the productions in exchange for the leading role. However, the shows all bombed. She has now attached herself to the lead role of The Innsmouth Terror. / Ginny has milky-white skin, and wears far too much makeup. Her bleached blonde hair is up in curls; her bright red dress is the same colour as her lipstick and she smells faintly of lavender. A closer look notes that slightly wide-set eyes, the slightly cracked skin and the slightly oversized teeth.

Anna Díaz, age 26, producer A technically brilliant, funny, well read, hard-working actress, Anna long ago gave up on her chances of ever making it big. The starring roles go to elegant, blond-haired bombshells, not solidlooking farm girls with dark brown skin and acne scars. / However, her near encyclopedic knowledge of the Arkham scene and her ability to sort out just about anything made her the perfect hire for producer of The Innsmouth Terror. Not that Anna has ever produced a film before, but she’s done plenty of stage shows and it can’t be that different, right? / It was Anna who sourced the old train cart that the crew are living in. She got it at a steal, and it’s far comfier than the tents that the crew would normally sleep in when on-site. It’s also been a complete life saver now that production is dragging on day after day, as there are no decent hotels in Innsmouth.

Sammy Brewster, age 21, dilettante & sibling A perfectly pleasant young white man from a rich family, Sammy is just starting to show the infamous Innsmouth look: his too large eyes and slightly fishy features make him more boyish than handsome; his slick blond hair gives off the impression of being slightly… damp. / Sammy has been hanging around the production camp trying to speak to his sister, Ginny. A couple of days ago, he was caught by the crew, who gave him the black eye he’s now sporting on his right eye. Ginny has made no move to contact him. She’s just not interested. / The Crew An unruly mob of heavyset men and women that do the lifting, the organizing, and occasionally play secondary roles in the film such as ‘Scary fish-man number 2’. They can mostly be found hanging around the production train or doing a variety of jobs around the set. Infinitely interchangeable and of indeterminate number, the Crew enjoy getting drunk and hanging around a fire pit in the evening. A simmering tension exists between the Crew and the residents of Innsmouth, and more than one fight has broken out between the groups.

START: ARKHAM / ORNE LIBRARY (MISKATONIC UNIVERSITY) / Our mystery opens in the quiet surroundings of the Orne Library in the Miskatonic University. The Society for the Exploration of the Unexplained (SEU) normally only meets once a month in a private reading room, but this unscheduled meeting has been quickly pulled together due to a request coming in from the Vice Chancellor of Miskatonic University themselves! The Vice Chancellor requires their help in recovering the Atlantean Jewel, a bizarre looking tiara made of alloyed gold (Handout 1-a: letter). It is the only one of its kind and an archaeological treasure. The note from the Board says little, other than to encourage the investigators to contact Diane Loring for further information.

rows.source_first_blocks: - On a successful Archaeology roll, investigators pull a little more information from Loring about the artifact. It is a tiara of an unusual gold alloy, one that modern science is unable to replicate. Such treasures are occasionally pulled up from the sea floor by fishermen, who then go on to sell them. This one is vaguely associated with the town of Innsmouth, which is why it was likely taken. / - Loring is not aware of any of the details of the film or its crew and recommends that investigators contact the local paper The Arkham Advertiser (adjacent) to find out more. She further mentions that, of course, the resources of the Orne Library are available to them should they need it. / Investigators may take many different avenues of research when using the Orne Library. To uncover general information about Innsmouth and the artifact, they can use a general Library Use roll. They may also use different avenues of research to come to some general conclusions about the theft:

rows.pdf_left_first_line: Investigators asking Karen for help get nothing for nothing,
rows.source_first_blocks: Investigators asking Karen for help get nothing for nothing, and Karen must be convinced with a successful Charm or Persuade roll, unless they bring her an exclusive story about how the Orne Library lost a priceless artifact. That interests her and she is then willing to share what she knows about the various players if the investigators are willing to provide an anonymous quote that would bring the great Miskatonic University into disrepute. / Once Karen does open up though, she is absolutely brimming with gossip about The Innsmouth Terror. / - The Director, P.A Bazzledon, appeared in Arkham about three weeks ago. He came up from New York, where his name is associated with a number of off-Broadway hits. It seems he’s a bit of a rising star.
Yours, / arKham / Handout 1-a: letter (See page 39 for Handout 1-b)

INNSMOUTH / ARRIVAL / The investigators can take the 9pm coach to Innsmouth from Dyer Street. It costs 40c and takes a little over 45 minutes. The coach itself is rickety and travels slowly, however, it drops them off in New Town Square, Innsmouth. Investigators with a car may instead choose to travel there in style. However, the road to Innsmouth is small, bumpy, and badly maintained. The driver should pass a Drive Auto roll or find they were driving too fast, blowing out the rear axle on the way to Innsmouth. They are then forced to hitch a ride with the bus anyway.

Innsmouth / THE GILMAN HOUSE HOTEL / The Gilman House is the infamous hotel from The Shadow over On Innsmouth by H.P. Lovecraft. Some groups may beeline straight It there, anticipating the horror, while others will do their utmost to avoid it.

rows.source_first_blocks: INVESTIGATION / THE PRODUCER’S OFFICE / It is early morning; though the sun is attempting to pierce its way through, it will be hours before it can burn off the mist blanketing the Manuxet valley. Anna Díaz sits at her crowded desk, retrofitted into a sleeping compartment of the Production Train. The smell of fresh coffee fills the room, the window is open, and birdsong can be heard in the distance. The investigators crowd into the remaining space of the room. There’s not enough room for them all to sit, and only one other chair.

rows.pdf_right_first_line: • Investigators trying to get into the mind of Bazzledon
rows.source_first_blocks: AROUND THE TRAIN / Set beside the sleeper car, attached to the antiquated steam engine, a diner car has been hastily converted into a number of large spaces. Entering from the steam engine side leads to Bazzledon’s Office (below), the center leads into Ginny’s Trailer (page 15), and the far side has a small ramp built into it that leads into McGuire’s Lab (page 16). All three doors are locked, requiring keys or a successful Lockpick roll. Once the investigators have access to one, the walls are cardboard thin and can be peeled back, allowing them to move between trailers. / Bazzledon’s Office The curtains are lazily pulled in this office, letting sharp beams of light cut through the dim, dusty haze. For the most part, Bazzledon is never in his office; instead he is always on set, shouting directions, making plans, and working to bring about the final scene, the culmination of his plans.

rows.source_first_blocks: Ginny’s Trailer Ginny’s trailer is bright, the windows open, catching a little of the sea breeze, intermingled with that fishy scent that seems to follow everything in Innsmouth. Alongside these familiar scents are spikes of strong perfumes. At first, the investigators might think that the place has been ransacked. Clothes cover every conceivable surface and the only clear floor space is around a large mirror, surrounded by incandescent bulbs. Even here, the discarded mascara brushes and dried-up make-up sponges are piled up and messy. It’s only possible to infer the location of the bed, as it is effectively just a pile of clothes at the far end of the room, almost a nest. / Underneath the mess, a fragmented car-crash of pink, frilly cushions and blood-red coverings are lazily arranged over modern, expensive-looking furnishings. As the investigators step in and around the mess, they choose to stand near the windows to survey the room, as the mixture of scents is drastically unpleasant. / Investigators trying to open the windows up further or passing a Spot Hidden roll find a scribbled note attached to the frame (Handout 2: note).

rows.source_first_blocks: McGuire’s Lab Wooden lab benches cover one entire length of this room, whilst on the other side, spikes are interspersed along the wall with heavy film roll hanging from them. Film is strewn just about everywhere, like a drunken spider’s web, and all the windows are blacked out by thick curtains. McGuire’s main workspace is lit by a pair of harsh incandescent bulbs without any lampshades. A partially disassembled camera is in pieces on the workbench. An investigator passing a Science (Engineering), or Electronic Repair roll marvels at the quality of workmanship that has gone into this camera. This truly is cutting edge technology. It seems to use a prism to split the light in two and then there are filters set up to record two identical scenes at the same time. / Though the lab may be messy, there’s not really anywhere to hide in it, and none of his drawers are locked. While investigators come across a wide variety of unsafe chemicals, they find no hidden treasures. / On McGuire’s desk, they find a short map of a cave system. Drawn using a ruler and many right-angles, it’s more of a conceptual cave map. However, the map seems to lead…. somewhere.

rows.pdf_right_first_line: Other than that, the remainder of the set is an empty field.
rows.source_first_blocks: On Set During the initial investigation, everyone involved in the production is working in a large open field beside the abandoned rail tracks. The weather today is dramatic, with stormy clouds threatening thunderstorms later, but for now there’s only a light breeze blowing. / This is likely the first opportunity the investigators have had to look over the dramatic landscape of Innsmouth. The valley below looks to be one extended swamp, but rising up above the far side of the town, jagged peaks and cliff faces give a feeling of enclosure and isolation. It’s hard to imagine that this lost bit of coastline is only a 45 minute bus ride from Arkham. Truly, modern technology is a marvel. / P.A Bazzledon and Christopher McGuire are quietly arguing over some technical points by the camera. Meanwhile, Ginny Dubois is resting on a foldable chair under a giant mink fur coat in a thick pair of sunglasses, while smoking from a cigarette holder. Two larger members of the Crew are sitting on the ground nearby, playing the dice game Twenty-Six. They are half-dressed as ‘frog-creatures’: their legs are made up to look scaly and wrong. Lying on the ground beside the Crew, there is a sort of plastic mold that looks like it covers a person’s torso, arms, and head, turning them into a plastic-y frog-like creature. At first glance, it’s a terrifying twisting of plastic lying haphazardly abandoned on the ground. It is only after the Crew get up and begin preparing for the scene that investigators truly comprehend it as a piece of costume.

The Railway Entrance A set of foreboding looking sharp rocks fall against one another creating a natural arch. Stepping through, a small grassy area with a lightly trodden path leads towards a slotted hole that runs down into some naturally forming tunnels. If investigators saw the glint of light while On Set (page 17), their eyes dart towards the broken binoculars lying on a rock. Otherwise, it requires a Spot Hidden to notice the binoculars. / If investigators have found Handout 2, they can follow the map instructions from here through The Cave System (below). It leads to The Brewster Residence (page 20). If they have no instructions and choose to enter the caves anyway, they exit the caves through an abandoned house in central Innsmouth. / THE CAVE SYSTEM

Table 2: encounters in the caves / | 1D100 | Description | | --- | --- | | 1-5 | What Luck: The Investigators discover a quick and easy route to wherever they are trying to get to. It feels like a great little caper scampering up and down between all these rocks. | | 6-10 | Footprints: The investigators spot fresh footprints, clear as day. On a successful Track roll, it’s clear they were made by someone wearing feminine shoes, likely of a similar build to Ginny or Anna. | | 11-20 | A Cracked Clue: Investigators uncover a discarded piece of metal on the ground. Clearing it of dust, they realize it has a similar sheen to the pictures of the Jewel. But it’s the wrong shape. On a successful Appraise roll, they determine it is gold alloy, likely valuable. | | 21-30 | A Foreboding Beach: The investigators get turned around and find themselves on a foreboding beach front. They’ll need to roll again. | | 31-40 | A Hole in the Wall: There is a hole in the wall and some dim light on the other side. Just big enough for someone to peep through with their eyes. The investigator holding the light has a penalty die on the roll. | | 91-95 | Watching Eyes: The investigator at the back of the group could swear they saw glowing eyes watching them from the shadows. They make a Sanity roll (0/1D4 loss) as they try to convince the others they are being followed. | | 96-100 | Close encounters: Stepping out onto a ledge, below the investigators the cave fills with water. Some creature is swimming down there lazily in the water. The investigators must quietly cross the ledge or risk disturbing the Deep One in the water. One investigator must pass a Stealth roll for the group or they must find another route and roll again. On failing the Stealth roll, a Deep One emerges from the water and attempts to eat the investigators. |

rows.source_first_blocks: THE BREWSTER RESIDENCE / Investigators can arrive at the Brewster Residence by emerging from the cave system. If they do, the exit is inside a mundane gardening shed in the front garden. Alternatively, they may find the address after speaking to Zadok Allen (The Fire Station, page 23). / In front of them stands a slightly dilapidated, though clearly still occupied, three-story house. Around the outside, the garden is overgrown and untended. On a successful Track roll investigators pick up a lightly worn track leading from the garden shed to a back window that doesn’t seem to shut properly. This window leads into Ginny’s old room.

rows.pdf_right_first_line: In reality, Bazzledon had in fact left the Jewel with McGuire.
rows.source_first_blocks: STUMBLING ONTO SET / Bright lights pain the eyes of the investigators as they round the corner into a scene of chaos. / In front of them, Bazzledon is shouting orders, McGuire is turning the camera arm, recording film. Behind a set of wooden sticks that might pass for jail-cell bars in bad light, Ginny is being dramatic, while a set of frog-like creatures poke and prod at her with primitive looking spears. The scene is disorienting for the investigators, whose eyes need a moment to adjust to the bright lights.

INTO INNSMOUTH / Inevitably, at some point, investigators will start asking questions around Innsmouth. They may simply begin asking after Sammy, or they may wish to see if they can definitively connect Ginny to Innsmouth. Investigators may instead begin looking to see if they can uncover any cults or otherwise malevolent forces in the town who may be interested in stealing the Jewel. / Innsmouth is an unfriendly town. Locals avoid going out into the street if they see the investigators passing, and many of the roads they walk through feel completely abandoned. Investigators can’t help but feel like they are being watched as they move through town and may occasionally spot queer glowing eyes following them from darkened windows.

The Fire Station Sitting on 100 Paine Street, not too far from the railway, the fire station isn’t immediately accessible to the investigators as they encounter a dangerous looking bridge made of rotting wood that doesn’t seem safe to cross. While it feels fine if the investigators cross it one at a time, anyone with a SIZ greater than 70 must pass a Luck roll or the rotten wood snaps, dropping the investigator into the Manuxet river, taking 1D6 damage and washing up three blocks down. The bridge certainly couldn’t hold the weight of a car, or the one operational fire engine, putting large portions of town at risk if the fire department was ever required (not that the damp, rotten wood of Innsmouth would necessarily burn all that well.) / Investigators looking for Zadok Allen find him here, resting himself against the stone outer wall of the fire station. It looks as if no one is manning the station today and he is all alone. / Zadok is grumpy, difficult, and uninterested in talking to a group of strangers at first. They need to loosen his lips with a bottle of whisky. However, if the investigators do tempt him with a tipple, he leads them away from the station, to a nice sheltered house on the edge of town looking out towards the cliff face.

The Esoteric Order of Dagon Speaking to Sammy or Zadok may lead the investigators to believe that the Jewel is connected to the Esoteric Order of Dagon. This is wrong; however if investigators get hooked into this pattern, the Keeper can encourage it, having them visit the Esoteric Order of Dagon. / Sitting prominently on Federal Street in the center of town, this neo-classical building is hard to miss. Four Grecian columns frame the main doorway, though the whitewash has faded to a dull gray. Above the door, a large stone carving of the words ‘Esoteric Order of Dagon’ stands prominently across the building. This building is a converted Masonic temple and is by far the grandest building in Innsmouth. / Four heavy-looking Hybrids lounge around the entranceway and they will stop the investigators if they try and approach the door directly. The Hybrids have a strong ‘Innsmouth Look’ about them and are quick to use a slap or gut punch to move on any investigators that seem overly inquisitive about temple matters.

the / THE EPIC FINALE / Once the investigation nears completion, and the investigators have a clear understanding that Ginny Dubois is the culprit, then the Epic Finale begins. This could happen anywhere around Innsmouth, though it is best for the moment to happen whilst the investigators are in town.
the epIc / MVR Class B1 ‘Olmstead’, steam locomotive MOV: 11 Build: 10 Armour for people: 1 / Gauge: standard (4 ft 8 1⁄2 in) Boiler pressure: 110

Playing the Hero / Investigators making their way determinedly up to the cliffs to the sacrifice experience no violent retribution from the Star- Spawn. In fact, the road clears ahead of them, as they rush up the winding path towards the climatic moment. The same events unfold if they are captured and brought up against their will. / As they approach, they see Christopher McGuire slowly turning the handle of the camera. His eyes are glazed and he is completely unresponsive. Ginny has been torn from the rock where she was tied, leaving behind a pentagram, clearly drawn in blood smeared across it. She is now in the clutches of the tentacles above, screaming for help. A number of Crew members lie in pieces around the site, their bodies seemingly torn to shreds by tentacles whilst attempting to save her.

They agree to the next 12 months funding up front. Further, the Society is offered a much nicer room for future meetings. One with a fireplace and far comfier seats usually reserved for faculty.
